catalog.rationale: Identifier referencing the parent BigLake catalog the database belongs to. It is a reference to another resource; we do not constrain resource names or references, so it is not a security policy target.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

name.rationale: Identifier/name of the table, database, or catalog resource. We do not constrain resource names, so it has no platform security policy.

type.rationale: Declares the object type (e.g. table/database type such as HIVE). This is a structural/compatibility descriptor, not a security control, so no policy is warranted.

hive_options.location_uri.description: Cloud Storage folder URI where the database data is stored, starting with "gs://".
hive_options.location_uri.rationale: A gs:// Cloud Storage path pointing at where the database/table data lives. This is a reference to another resource (a bucket/folder); we secure the bucket itself elsewhere and do not constrain references to it, and a generic policy can't validate an arbitrary path without hardcoding. Exposure/residency is enforced on the bucket's own public-access and location controls, not this pointer.

hive_options.parameters.description:
Stores user supplied Hive database parameters. An object containing a
list of"key": value pairs.
Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }.
hive_options.parameters.rationale: Free-form key/value Hive metadata parameters for the table or database. This is an arbitrary metadata map; a generic policy cannot meaningfully constrain free-form parameters, so it is not a useful policy target.
